This is a very nice hair serum that is targeted at encouraging and speeding up hair growth. The first ingredent, and therefore the  most prevalent ingredient, is a type of silicone. Silicone has become the most popular ingredient for anti-friz and shine serums for hair, not to mention a whole world of cosmetics like oil free moisturizers and foundations. It has a slip to it, which gives silicone the *feeling of being like an oil, but it is by its nature, is totally oil free. And of course, also by its nature, it cannot clog pores or follicles. The active ingredients in the product, or the ingredients that actually enable the product to do its job of encouraging hair growth, are Jojoba Oil, Macadamia Nut Oil, Lupine Protein, and Panax Ginseng. These nourish and stimulate the hair follicles to remain longer in the anagen, or hair growing phase, and to produce healthier, stronger hair from the root. Jojoba oil is a skin compatible oil, meaning that it cannot and does not clog pores or follicles, closely resembles the body's own natural lubrication, and can be absorbed by human hair, skin, and nails. There is also extract of Macadamia Nut Oil, which moisturizes the hair cuticle and shaft and helps to prevent hair breakage and split ends. Hydrolyzed protein from the seeds of the lupine plant are very high in protein and contain 35-45% of all the essential amino acids. Panax ginseng is an extract from the panax ginger root and has nourishing and stimulating qualities that directly feed and nourish the hair follicle. This Mat Wins Over Bundle Monster, Ejiubas & Bliss Kiss! I have this mat, the Bundle Monster mat, and the Ejiubas mat, and this one wins first place in terms of overall quality! It drives me crazy that it doesn't have any black areas for stamping & whatnot (thus, the deduction of one star), but its value, its reasonably sized nail guides, and best of all, the softness of the silicone makes this one the superior choice in my opinion.

DESIGN

In terms of design, I believe the other two mats are superior over Uber Chic, although UC's isn't bad. Bundle Monster's Lotus Mat is my favorite, but I'm also partial to lotus flowers ;) Its nail guides are ridiculously large, though, but it *does* have black sections to practice on, so that's a huge plus.

The Ejiubas mat has a pretty cool & very unique layout compared to all other mats, with its nail sizing grids in both black and white, while still leaving plenty of empty space to work on.

One thing I do love about the UC mat is the amount of empty space it features. Some mats out there that I haven't mentioned here are SO busy with verbiage & useless "features" that it's a huge turn off. Less is definitely more!

VALUE

With regard to value, Ejiubas wins, hands down. I purchased mine for $13, and it came with a great little carry bag! Bundle Monster loses miserably in this category. And, Uber Chic falls somewhere in the middle, which makes its value "okay" in my opinion.

TEXTURE - THE DEAL-BREAKER!

The (negative) deal-breaker for me is the stickiness of the other two mats. And as a disclaimer, I'm using the word "sticky," although it's not literally sticky... Rubbery is probably a better word, but I'm going with sticky ;)

So, I can't stand how *everything* sticks to the Ejiubas mat to the point that you can't even blow or fan debris off of it with your hand. This means it always feels like it needs to be cleaned, it's difficult to keep clean, and actually cleaning it is kind-of a pain.

The Bundle Monster mat falls somewhere between Ejiubas and Uber Chic in terms of stickiness. It's much better than the Ejiubas mat, but still sticky enough to be plenty annoying.

The Uber Chic mat, though? It's heavenly smooth :) I love it! It's very soft, and very easy to keep clean. Absolutely zero complaints on that front.

CONCLUSION

If Uber Chic would add some black stamping sections, this mat would be absolutely flawless in my opinion. Every mat out there seems to have at least one superior and one inferior feature that makes it difficult to choose the "best" one.

If it were up to me, I'd use the Uber Chic mat with the Bundle Monster design, except with Uber Chic's nail guide sizes, and Ejiubas' price point & free carry bag. Maybe I'll just have to make one of these, so I can finally have the perfect silicone nail art mat! ;)

Good product, excellent customer service! I'm not new to hair extensions. I've worn them for a few years quite a while ago when growing out a short cut. My hair is currently color treated dark red at the roots and the color fades to magenta at the ends. I got the light brown to blonde extensions so I could custom dye them to match. The extensions took the dye very well and you can't tell a color difference between my hair and the extensions at all.

The claim that they are thick from root to tip isn't true. Most extensions claim this though and I expected it, so I got longer hair than I really wanted so I could trim it and get rid of the thinning in the ends. I've had minimal shedding so all in all, that is a plus.

They come super straight out of the pack but have some natural wave to them when you wash them. Not a problem as my natural hair does too so they blend well there too. They are soft and as long as you use a leave in oil they will stay frizz free. They hold curl really well too. I curled them and they stayed curled over two days, long after the curl fell out of my natural hair. I've had some tapes separate after install, and removed some due to my own misplacement, but replaced them with tape I had before. Most of the original tape has been replaced at this point so I can't speak to its quality or longevity.

I'm not totally blown away but am happy enough with my purchase to wear them until it's time to replace them.

I love the minimal ingredient list (Purified Water (Aqua), Sodium Olivate, Glycerin, Rosa Rubiginosa (Rose Hip) Seed Oil, Eriobotrya, Japonica Extract, Chondrus Crispus (Seaweed) Extract).

This product seems to be all around quite mild. The scent is lightly floral, not overly pleasant or unpleasant, not too strong and doesn’t linger. The lather is present but not super foamy. Most importantly for me, the product has not CAUSED any irritation. I have really sensitive skin, and I have not noticed any additional drying or breakouts due to using this product. However, I also haven’t noticed any particularly hydrating or clearing effects either. My skin does feel rather smooth and fresh since using this wash, but I find that I still need several other facial products to achieve this.

I was a bit concerned with the directions stating to avoid the eye area, because many of the healthy-skin and anti-aging benefits of the ingredients in this product would be ideal for the eye area, and I was initially hoping to use this as a make-up removing cleanser. However, I adhered to the directions, and I do not use this as a make-up removing cleanser, and only use it following or prior to make-up removal/application. The good news is, while I don’t directly put this product on my eyes, I am not super careful about avoiding the eye area while rinsing and I have not experienced any stinging or eye discomfort as I have with several similar products in the past.

Overall, I found this to be a pretty good product, I like it quite a bit but I didn’t find it to be a particularly extraordinary product either. I do recommend this product to others as a part of their beauty regimen, but I definitely need (and recommend others) to use a make-up remover prior to use, and a moisturizer following use, so this isn’t a one-and-done type product.

This is the standard by which all other shave soaps are measured MWF was one of the first soaps I discovered early on when I returned to DE shaving, and after I figured out how to get it lathered - it’s been a great baseline to use as a comparison point to other vendor’s products. It is listed as unscented, and with the exception of a lanolin scent - it is.
Lather:
MWF is known to be difficult to lather. The trick seems to be dialing in the water amount (usually more than other shave soaps) that it needs to properly lather. However, once you’ve figured out how to dial it in for your specific water - it is easy to repeat your success in subsequent shaves. Hint – a good brush makes a WORLD of difference here… Do I want to take this camping, or use it in the field – No. Too much work to lather and uses too much water (a heavy resource to pack in). At home where I have a sink and running water - it’s fine.
Slickness:
When properly lathered, MWF is one of the slickest soaps I’ve ever used. For several years I have used it as the baseline when evaluating other shave soaps slickness. I don’t know if it’s the lanolin, or the extra amount of water required to get it lathered that makes it so slick, but by goodness it works. The best part is that when properly lathered, the slickness lasts and does not dry out too quickly. I can lather my entire face at the beginning of my shave, and not be rushed to complete it before the lather dissipates.

NOT a nail buffer - this is a file - worth maybe $8 so way over-priced
A nail buffer requires a very, very, very fine grit so it will polish and shine the nail. This supposed buffer is medium grit, which means it is good for filing nail edges and maybe ok for removing ridges from the nail surface if you use very light pressure, but it will not polish the nail top surface - i.e. despite the name, this is a file.  When used on the nail top surface, it mostly produces scratches. Even if the grit on this file was fine enough, it is too wide to properly polish the small curved surface of a nail (I am not talking thickness/height here, I mean width).  Plus decorative top is just glued on.  I have tried so many glass nail buffers that I have lost count - all were too wide and too coarse to actually buff the nail except one - the one that actually had a fine enough grit was so wide that it could only polish my nails in spots.  I would love a long-lasting glass nail buffer, but at this point my conclusion is that glass is not suitable for buffing because it is too rigid and all supposed glass buffers available are very badly designed.  I give up.  I guess I will continue with disposable 4-sided soft block buffers - at least those work properly.  Gave the file to my niece as she loves the appearance of it and it is good for filing (properly etched, medium grit), just way over-priced at $13 and NOT as described.

It only made my hair a little softer.... I bought this at Sally Beauty. I am caucasion, in my 50's with blonde/gray fine hair that is straight with some body & has never been colored or bleached; length is 2" below my shoulders.
My hair has been very dry for a long time despite lots of moisturizing, a salon keratin treatment (cha-ching!), argon oil, deep conditioning, etc... This Aphogee two-step protein treatment was recommended to me at the Sally Beauty store, and I figured it was worth a try. I followed the instructions to a T & also watched lots of youtube videos. I used this today exactly as directed & with high hopes. I shampooed & towel-dried my hair, then applied protein treatment, blow dried my hair for 12 minutes w/ the protein treatment in it, then rinsed in shower with warm water followed by the balancing moisturizer for at least 2 minutes, rinsed & used a moisturizing hair mask ("Mystic Divine" Coconut Complex Hydrating Masque), then rinsed again. My hair felt softer, at first, but my frizzies & curly gray hairs are still sticking out all over. I didn't get any more body in my hair either (my keratin treatment was last year 2017). So, all in all it is okay as a moisturizer, but no better than a regular deep moisture conditioner or mask. I'm not sure if I would use it again, maybe. I'm glad I just got the sampler size.
Here are my tips:
1) Use a spray mister bottle for the protein liquid & make sure you get out every last drop from the packet because most of it came out as beer colored water, then at the bottom of the packet was more of a thick cream, so I shook them together in the spray bottle & I'm so glad I used that! Don't just pour it on your head, at the very least pour a little into your hands at a time (after massaging the packet to mix contents) and smooth through your hair that way. There was just enough for my hair length.
2) Don't put a towel or anything around your shoulders, no clothing either because the protein treatment will dry your hair to it. Don't pull your stuck hairs off your skin, they'll come unattached in the shower, no worries. I kept my hair behind me to apply treatment & blow dry.
3) After drying the protein into your hair, don't touch your hair or bend it, (you can very gently touch lightly with your finger, if you hair wasn't already super brittle; it will feel like plastic sort of. 4) Be very careful blow-drying; I pointed the dryer downward alternating between medium & high heat & kept it farther from my hair so it wasn't blowing it around as it hardened. When hair is totally hard & dried through then gently let the shower water fall over all of your hair until you feel no more stiffness, then you can condition.
It's worth a try! The packets were just under $4 at Sally Beauty if you want to try it, or order here on Amazon.

Super underrated fragrance house English Laundry is highly underrated. It's fine to call them what they are, they're a relatively cheapy house that makes fragrances that are often inspired by others, but they do it very well. I have more than a few of their scents and this is what you can expect of these four:

Notting Hill - This has what you might call a barbershop scent to it. A strong, clean musk, definitely some wood notes in there with a mix of cedar and sandalwood. I've heard it compared to Viking by Creed and I think that's not far off on the dry down, but the opening on Notting Hill has more citrus. Strongest scent of the bunch for sure.

Riveria - This is just a great, easily wearable blue fragrance. I gave mine another spray while I writing this just for the reminder. I was surprised when I first smelled this because this was THE scent from English Laundry that was hyped up. And I like it, no question, but it's very similar to other blue scents. It dries down powdery, has a hint of woodsy notes, but I mostly just get lavender and jasmine mixing with a bit of aquatic notes. That said, it's unbeatable at it's price and probably the easiest to wear in the bunch.

Oxford Bleu - So, when I first smelled this I thought "Oh that's just straight up Versace Eros." Having smelled them side by side since I own them both, it's still very similar, but a little different. Eros is more loud, Oxford Bleu has a lot of the same mint, vanilla, and apple that you'd get from Eros, but more subdued in the dry down. Again, for the price you can't go wrong here, it's an exceptional scent, but that's because Eros is an exceptional scent.

Arrogant - A disclaimer upfront: I think what's going on with Arrogant and me is all just my personal body chemistry. It's a sleeper hit for sure, it has a very clean, soapy, lavender feel to it that I love. The only problem is that unless I over spray, the scent dies on my skin really fast. It's not a complaint I've heard elsewhere, so this might just be me, but that gives it a disappointment mark or two. I went and put this on a tester strip as I was writing this and could barely smell it, so I put a couple of sprays on my skin, and sure, I definitely like it, but it's hard to pick up with normal use. I might just be nose blind to it, honestly. The closest scent I could place it with would be Le Male by John Paul Gaultier. Just a bit weaker.

All in all, English Laundry is not to be slept on, and there's no bad scents in this bunch.

Nice improvement This is a nice improvement to the Sonicare line of brushes. It appears to be their response to the Oral-B Floss Action line of brushes that have a "paddle" to help get between teeth. This accomplishes that goal with an plastic insert in the middle that helps direct the toothpaste between your teeth.

I use both the Sonicare (Healthy White) and the Oral B 5000. Both have their pluses and minuses, so switching between the two gives me the best of both worlds.

The Oral-B arrangement of paddles does a better job in getting at the gum line without discomfort. The Sonicare Hydroclean's bristles are stiffer and I find that they irritate my gums when used several times in a row.

But, the Sonicare does a better job in cleaning stains between teeth. I'm a tea drinker and getting the stains out between my front teeth has always been a chore. The Hydroclean works very well - noticeable improvement over the Sonicare ProResults and the Oral-B.

These only come in the standard size. The ProResults has a smaller version that is great for getting at the tight spots. But, I assume that a smaller version of this would not function well since the plastic insert would have to be very small.

If you're a ProResults user these are well worth trying out. If you have tender gums you may want to alternate between the HydroClean and the ProResults (or, as I do, with the Oral-B. The Oral-B also makes a super soft brush if you have very sensitive gums. Hard to find, but works very well).

Keep in mind that nothing takes the place of flossing. No matter what you use, you still need to break out the floss to keep your teeth healthy!

Just can't do its job I want to believe in a world in which redemption is always possible. There should be no unforgivable sins; your better qualities should always offer the hope that your failings, however profound, can be overcome.

But this shaver fails in the single unforgivable way that an electronic device can: despite lots of bells and whistles, it doesn't do the one thing you purchase it to do.

I bought this to replace an older model Norelco wet/dry shaver that finally gave up the ghost. This razor offers some additional features my old one lacked: it's much lighter, holds a charge longer, and has a silly and totally unnecessary shave-goo-dispensing system built into it. I tried to find a wet/dry Norelco shaver with no "moisturizing system," but to no avail. If you want to shave in the shower, Norelco wants to insure you keep purchasing more shave gel cartridges. After reading some reviews that suggested the shaver worked perfectly well without it squirting glop everywhere, I was satisfied this was the right purchase.

Unfortunately, the shaver is unsatisfactory in one way: it just doesn't shave very well. I've used it on my face and head, with and without moisturizer, wet and dry, and its shave is pretty lousy. My old Norelco provided a shave that was very smooth and comparable to a blade; with this model, there's noticeable beard fuzz left behind immediately after I shave, and by the end of the day, I look like I forgot to shave at all that morning. When I found myself going back over my face with a regular razor right after I used the 8040X, I knew this shaver had to go. I would like to believe that its lightweight, comfortable form and good battery life could redeem it, but sadly, its transgression is too profound. I may not be able to forgive it, but I'm pretty sure I'll forget I ever owned it before long.

Process:
The process was actually pretty fun. I’ve noticed people complain that it’s still sticky after using the LEDUV light, but I have found that I have to use the light about 3 times for each nail for it to fully cure. You have to apply it pretty thick for them to last a while. The thinner the poly gel, the more likely it will break off easier.

Results:
The results were very cute! The nails only lasted a couple of hours though as 2 nails broke off after I took a shower, but I have a feeling it was because it was my first time and I applied the poly gel fairly thinly.

THE BEST! Better than Super Blue, Glam Seamless Tape, and Satin Strands. Try it! I have had tape-in extensions for several years and these are BY FAR the BEST replacement tapes I have used. I only use Glam Seamless extension hair and these fit those pieces really well. I love that these can easily be split in half because when I place my extensions I use a single piece and fold it in half, rather than sandwiching 2 pieces, to put less weight on my baby fine hair.

I have tried many types of replacement tapes including the "Super Blue", and in a pinch the super cheap (quality, not cost!) Satin Strands, and these far outshine them all. With all other tapes I always lose 1-2 pieces every time I wash my hair (which is only 1x/week), and the rest slip a little with each wash. So because of that I always put them in as close to the scalp as possible. To my surprise, not only did I not lose any with this tape, they didn't slip at all, not even a little! So I had nearly 2 weeks of my extensions remaining really tight to my head! I almost pulled them out because they were getting uncomfortable, but I ended up sticking it out.

It has now been just about 6 weeks and I am going to pull them out and reset them within the week. They still haven't slipped very much, and I still haven't lost a single one! By this point with any other tape, half of them would have come out by now! I could easily leave these in another month without much issue, but my baby fine hair knots easily when there is any outgrowth.

This tape is a little bit thicker than other tapes, which is likely why it holds so well. When putting the two pieces together, really press down and squish them together to ensure there is a secure contact with both sides. Then heat set the pieces between a hot iron on low for 5-10 seconds - this is not in the instructions but is recommended on the product's website, so I did it, and got really great results!

Because these have such a strong hold, I just ordered the C-22 solvent to remove them. I normally use coconut oil, but suspected I might need something a bit more to remove these. I will update my review once I remove them and share whether or not it was more difficult, compared to other tapes.

This works great! You just have to know how to use it correctly. The double curler band allows you to use less hair on each curler so that the hair dries faster and curls faster. Here IS MY 2 HOURS TO PRETTY CURLS METHOD: Part upper hair at crown of head,  and put hair from the upper head at crown,  in a pony tail for later. Snap the curling system closed, so that there is 2 round circle bands to use to curl with, and put both around head like a double crown head band. Push the top curling band where pont tail is for later use. Separate the bottom layer of hair into two parts... left side and right side and use only the bottom circle band curler for the bottom portion of head. Begin curling in left side by spritzing a little water onto the hair at root and curl it under band tucking it under and around curler one time only and then in next pass, grab a little more hair with it and continue going around the curler band. Keep spritzing new hair with water each time you pick up a new piece of hair and add that hair to the previous end of the one you just curled, until the whole left, bottom  side is done. Then start on the bottom right side of hair. When finished,  the  whole bottom curling band  will be filled with the hair from the lower portion of. Now it's time to take out the pony tail that was  on the grown of head  and put that hair under the second curling band and separate the left side of hair from the right. Start curling the left upper part of head as you did the bottom portion... spritzing small portion of hair with water at root and curling it once around the band and then pick up a little more new hair, spritz it with water and curl together with the former portion around band until all left side is done and now do right side. DO NOT SOAK HAIR.  Only LIGHTLY MIST IT a little with water or it wont dry in 2 hours. Dont curl too big a portion of hair at a time either, or it won't dry in two hours. Wait about 1 hour to 2 hours and remove curlers and you will get beachy type ringlets that are big. It takes about 10 minutes to wind hair around curlers. Lovely curls.

Great trimmer I've had this trimmer for probably 6+ years and it is still going strong. Just a hint if you have one and are looking to replace the G380 due to battery loss give this a try once a year:
Run until the battery discharges fully. By this I mean when the battery is getting weak I take the attachments off and turn on the power switch. Leave the switch on until the gizmos stop rotating then turn off. Wait about 20 minutes or so and then power on to deplete the rest of the battery (you can try this a few times to make sure it is fully drained). After discharging, plug it into the charger and let fully charge (I think I let mine charge overnight). This unit is now back to original power, and I haven't had to recharge in over 3 weeks of normal use and it functions like new). Just a tip to save you some money before deciding to buy another unit which I almost did. I could not find a replacement battery when I thought the battery was the issue.

cat LOVES the brush, but hated it initially.. When I first opened this brush I was very excited to see how my spoiled cat would like a nice brushing with it. I pulled it out of the package and showed it to him as he needs to inspect everything before he will allow it near him. He unfortunately ran away as soon as he got one sniff! I was puzzled, but I quickly realized that the silicone was not smelling great. That sometimes happens with new silicone and it just needs to sit out for a few days to have the smell dissipate. In a couple days the smell went away and I gave the brush another try. At first my cat pulled away because he remembered the smell, but once he realized it didn't smell, he let me give him a pet. He generally likes gentle petting, but this brush by nature makes even the most gentle brushing a little more rough. He accepted the new level of brushing and I proceeded to brush him. I was immediately amazed at the amount of cat hair this brush was removing per brush. This hands down is the most efficient cat brush I have ever used! I had to clean the bristles every few strokes, which is very simple to do by peeling the hair off in one large section. My cat is a short hair and does not shed very much at all, so I was confused as to how so much hair was being removed from my cat. He was in heaven so I kept on going until each section I was brushing would not brush out any more hair. When he got up from brushing, the cat looked better to me. Maybe because all of the loose hair was no longer holding down his shiny Tuxedo hair. In all I took out a handful of hair from my 7 pound cat. His coat looks shinier, fluffier and healthier now because of a simple brushing.

One thing I do need to mention about this brush is that it is not the most comfortable thing to hold for long periods of time. I pet my cat for about 45 minutes and my hand was hurting from gripping the cube for so long.

I removed 1 star - for the initial smell and the uncomfortable hand grip.

Colonoscopy Prep NECESSITY I recently had my first colonoscopy, and I had been warned that the prep was the worst part. Yeah, that was a total understatement. I am SO grateful to my mom, who told me to lay in a supply of this Balneol lotion to use when ... um ... tidying up after eliminating.

I will admit, I was skeptical. Lotion? For my BUM?! Turns out, that's a very definite YES.

If you've had a colonoscopy, you know that after you drink that concoction of vileness that they call the "prep drink," you're going to poop in much the same way that Vesuvius erupts. Trip after trip to the loo, right? Right. Oh, you thought you were done and could have a little lie-down to recover? Haha. NOPE! Why don't you just bring in War and Peace and sit here the rest of the day?

So after a few trips to the throne room, your bum feels a bit sore. Even the softest toilet tissue feels like 80-grit sandpaper rasping all the skin off your most delicate bits. And you can't stop going to the loo, because that death-potion you had to drink is ripping through you like a wildfire through a summer-dry grassland. In fact, your bum feels like it might BE on fire.

That's where this lotion stuff comes in. After gently patting the worst of the debris off your bum, you take a fresh piece of toilet roll and put a bit of this stuff on it. Use that to clean up the rest of you. The relief is instant, like a cup of ice-water after a mid-day hike through Death Valley in mid-August. And it does seem to make the cleanup more effective.

I imagine people with chronic digestive issues would also find this useful, and I know that on days when my "girl thing" is happening, it's a relief to clean up using this product. But if you're slated for a colonoscopy, you should most definitely lay in a supply of this stuff. You're gonna need it!

Look great, easy to apply, hard to remove I'm a false eyelash beginner and I have to say that magnetic lashes are far easier to apply, in my opinion, because the magnetic pull as you get the lashes close to their intended destination help you place them properly. They also seem to be a little more forgiving than traditional adhesive lashes if you need to slightly reposition them. This set has a great variety of styles and lengths and comes with two tubes of magnetic liner and a pair of eyelash calipers to help set them in place. If you're just starting out with lashes, this is a great way to do it.

However, there are some downsides. First, I find the eyeliner extremely irritating to my eyes (and my nose, as it is heavily scented). It is also really difficult to remove (I have to soak my eyelids with Bi-Facil on a cotton pad at least twice and then follow up with micellar water and MAYBE that will get all of it off). Be prepared to soak your lashes, because that's the only way this stuff is coming off. Second, I find the lashes somewhat uncomfortable. They feel heavier on the lid than adhesive lashes and I can often feel the metal on the band. I tend to remove these long before I remove a pair of adhesive lashes because I am never NOT aware of them on my lids. Third, if you use a tweezer/caliper thing to place your lashes, do yourself a favor and just buy a decent one. This one is plastic and has no tension, so you have to manually open it to fix the lashes in it, then fiddle with it again to take it away from the lashes. For me this was a bonus, because I got so frustrated with it, I just learned to do it with my hands with much better results.

Despite my problems with this set, I would totally recommend trying this out to see if magnetic lashes are for you. The variety of styles will give you a lot of options to experiment with different looks, but do take care of your eyelids and make sure you have appropriate product to remove the tenacious eyeliner. Happy lashing!

This package comes with a squeeze bottle full of a very pleasant smelling lotion, that you inject into the back of the shaver. Then, when you are shaving, you just press a button and it releases enough lotion to lubricate about one third of the face. When it starts to feel like a dry shave, you press the button again and finish up.

I have found that the amount of lotion you can inject into the shaver is enough for about 5 to 6 shaves. The shaver comes with a small sample bottle of the lotion -- and I guess one drawback is that you have to keep buying the lotion, unless you want to use this like an ordinary dry shaver. I've tried that too and it seems to work as well as any other shaver I've tried. I prefer, though, to use the lotion. It feels good and has a nice aftershave smell that my wife also likes -- that's good enough for me.

Because the system is water resistant, you can shave in the shower, and you can wash it off in water when you are finished. The extendable trimmer isn't very useful, but I've never seen a shaver where they are. It comes fully recharged and after about two weeks of using it about every other day it is still working well -- I haven't charged it yet. I do wish there was some kind of indicator on the unit that would let me know how much charge remains, but all in all I am quite happy with this.

Doesn't do anything that a reused margarine tub doesn't do Thanks to a series of unfortunate events involving a car accident AND a bike accident, I am the (not so) proud owner of a partial denture. For quite a while, I just used two old margarine tubs to soak my denture. (Pro tip: soak your denture in plain water in a separate container and then rinse it thoroughly before putting it in the cleaning solution, and then your cleaning solution won't get nasty.) But when the lids of my margarine tubs started to crack, I decided to get some "real" denture cups. Yeah...I should have just eaten some more margarine and washed out a new tub.

These cups are not in the least impressive. The lid of the blue cup snaps shut but isn't remotely leakproof--tip it just slightly and you'll have water or cleaning solution sloshing all over. The lid of the white cup doesn't even snap shut. It just barely rests on top of the cup and strainer, and if you don't watch what you're doing when you pick up the container, you'll find yourself holding the lid and looking at the cup and water/solution all over the floor. Furthermore, the two cups are far too hard to stack. The white one can't go on top of the blue one because the lid of the blue one is curved, but putting the blue one on top of the white one is precarious because the blue one is wider. And I find it surprisingly annoying to have two containers that won't stack taking up twice as much space as necessary in my tiny bathroom. About the only feature of these cups that is at all handy is the little strainer thing, and since my denture is plastic and floats, I don't find even that feature very useful.

Bottom line: you can soak dentures in pretty much any container, and you can find two small plastic containers with flat tops and secure lids for considerably less than the cost of these. Toast with margarine, anyone?

Good trims, flimsy parts I read all the reviews and decided to take a chance, based on the past good performance of an older Norelco trimmer.

The good news is that this trimmer works as well as the old Norelco and its small mustache trimmer attachment is much better than the one-size-fits-all blade of earlier models.

The charging and battery indicator systems are also very much improved.

The vacuum feature, which I did not expect to be perfect, is adequate, but as others have said, don't buy just for that. It appears to catch more than half the mess, which is helpful.

My only complaint is the parts you need to work with every time you use the trimmer. The detachable comb/accu-trim guide is not flimsy per se, but the tracks it fits into are and it requires careful attention to align it properly to put it back on the trimmer. I fear that one of these days I may put it on outside the track and snap the plastic runners that go into the tracks.

The internal pieces of the cutter mechanisms -- main and mustache trimmer -- are downright flimsy. The first time I removed the main blade it felt like something snapped, but I couldn't see anything wrong. When I put it back on after using the mustache trimmer, the device ran at about half RPM and sounded like it was straining. Sure enough, the force required to remove the main blade had resulted in its inner row of teeth coming out of the little track it runs in, back and forth, to cut hair, and I had to play jeweler as I squinted to carefully coax it back into place.

Not having owned any other brand, I don't know if they cut any better -- I doubt it. But the older Norelco was less fragile.

I plan to keep this one, unless it breaks during the 60-day trial. If I could rate it at 3.5 stars I would.

UPDATE Feb. 21: nothing has broken; the "problem" parts are wearing in so they come apart much more easily and I am definitely going to keep this trimmer.
